desc:
The string s consists of lowercase English letters. The vowels are a, e, i, o, u; every other letter is a consonant.

Return the length of the longest substring that contains at most k consonants (counting repeated consonants each time they occur).

s = "education", k = 1
"atio" has one consonant (t)
result = 4
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Replace each letter by 1 if it is a consonant and 0 if it is a vowel. You want the longest stretch whose total is at most k.
Adding a character to a substring never reduces its consonant count, so the rule is monotone: once a window is invalid, only dropping characters from the left can repair it.
Slide a window: extend right, add one to the consonant count when needed, and while the count exceeds k move left forward (subtracting when you leave a consonant).
editorial: The condition is about a count that only grows as the window grows, so a two-pointer sweep applies. For every right end the best left end is the smallest index for which the window still has at most k consonants, and that left end never decreases as right increases.

Maintain the number of consonants inside the window. After adding s[right] shrink the window while the count is above k, then update the best length. When k = 0 the answer is the longest run of vowels. Time O(n), space O(1).
